entities.name: PMID:25080093
observations: Gladstone and Vach (2014) observational study of registered and published non-inferiority trials.
Included 112 binary-outcome, 38 continuous-outcome, and 24 survival-outcome non-inferiority trials.
Translated each non-inferiority margin into the conditional probability that treatment is harmful given a declaration of non-inferiority, using simulation.
Median likelihood of degradation was 56% (lower/upper quartile 45%/62%).

Only about two-fifths of trials had degradation likelihood below 50%; authors concluded current margin choices generally did not sufficiently protect against average degradation and proposed a third hurdle for margin selection.

entities.name: NI margin degradation risk
observations: Across current-practice non-inferiority trials, the median modeled probability of a harmful treatment being declared non-inferior was 56%, indicating insufficient average protection from degradation.

entities.name: Third hurdle for NI margins
observations: The authors proposed adding a third hurdle to non-inferiority margin selection to ensure a sufficient degree of protection against degradation, beyond existing margin-selection considerations.
